title: From Text to Vision to Voice Exploring Multimodality with Open AI: Romain Huet

summary: Romain Huet, who leads developer experience at OpenAI, frames the talk around OpenAI's multimodality evolution. OpenAI's mission is building AGI that benefits all humanity, achieved through iterative deployment that puts technology in contact with reality early and often. Developers are central; OpenAI now has 3 million developers on its platform. The first OpenAI product was the developer API, launched in 2020 with GPT-3, enabling coding assistance, copy editing, translation, and text-based games like AI Dungeon. GPT-4 in 2023 transformed reasoning, creativity, coding, and tool use, and began the multimodality journey with image interpretation. GPT-4 Turbo integrated vision into the same model. GPT-4o ("o" for omni) unifies audio, video, and text in a single model, eliminating the previous pipeline of stitching Whisper, GPT-4, and text-to-speech, which caused context loss and latency. GPT-4o is twice as fast as GPT-4 Turbo, half the price, and has 5x higher rate limits. Huet demos live scenarios via ChatGPT Desktop (option+space): voice mode with natural latency, emotion understanding, and interruptibility; camera mode identifying a hand-drawn Golden Gate Bridge, translating French text, recognizing Poor Charlie's Almanack, and summarizing page 126; and screen sharing where ChatGPT reviews a travel app's mobile responsiveness, suggests Tailwind CSS media queries with the SM prefix, and analyzes a React use_assistant hook. He then outlines four future focus areas: textual intelligence (models are the dumbest they'll ever be), faster and cheaper models (GPT-4 pricing dropped 80% in a year, batch API offers 50% discount), model customization (fine-tuning API, Harvey customizing GPT-4 on US case law), and agents (Devin from Cognition Labs as example). Huet demos Sora generating a tree frog documentary video, slices frames and sends them to GPT-4 with vision to generate narration, then feeds that narration script into Voice Engine to create a custom voice clone of himself speaking in English, French, and Japanese. He closes emphasizing OpenAI's goal is for developers to build more, not spend more, and that this is the most exciting time to build AI-native companies.
whyItMatters: The talk connects its engineering abstractions, implementation choices, and AI/product implications into one practical system view.

sections.title: Introduction and OpenAI Mission
sections.summary: Romain Huet introduces himself as head of developer experience at OpenAI, outlines the AGI mission, iterative deployment philosophy, and the centrality of developers (3 million on the platform).

sections.title: History: From GPT-3 to GPT-4o
sections.summary: Retrospective from GPT-3 API (2020, first product) with text-only use cases like AI Dungeon, through GPT-4 (2023) with reasoning and image interpretation, GPT-4 Turbo with integrated vision, to GPT-4o omni model unifying audio, video, and text.

sections.title: GPT-4o Step Function Changes
sections.summary: GPT-4o replaces the three-model voice pipeline (Whisper + GPT-4 + TTS) with a single model, achieving 2x speed vs GPT-4 Turbo, half the price, and 5x rate limits.

sections.title: Live Demo: Voice Mode
sections.summary: ChatGPT Desktop voice demo showing natural latency, emotion understanding (whispering, energetic greetings), interruptibility, and conversational flow at the AI Engineer World's Fair.

sections.title: Live Demo: Camera Vision
sections.summary: Camera mode demo: ChatGPT identifies a hand-drawn Golden Gate Bridge, translates French text, recognizes Poor Charlie's Almanack, and summarizes page 126 about Coco Chanel in real time.

sections.title: Live Demo: Screen Sharing and Code Review
sections.summary: Screen sharing demo: ChatGPT reviews a travel app's mobile responsiveness, identifies layout issues, suggests Tailwind CSS SM prefix media queries, and analyzes a React use_assistant hook. Huet notes ChatGPT Desktop can be used as a coding assistant and even to generate prompts for Cursor.

sections.title: Future Focus Areas: Intelligence, Cost, Customization, Agents
sections.summary: Huet outlines four focus areas: textual intelligence (models are the dumbest they'll ever be, expected to become like master students), faster and cheaper models (GPT-4 pricing down 80% in a year, batch API 50% discount, more model sizes planned), model customization (fine-tuning API, Harvey customizing GPT-4 on US case law), and agents (perceiving and interacting with the world, Devin from Cognition Labs as example).

sections.title: Live Demo: Sora Video Generation and GPT-4 Vision Narration
sections.summary: Huet demos Sora generating a tree frog documentary video from a text prompt, then slices frames and sends them to GPT-4 with vision to generate a unique real-time narration of what it sees.

sections.title: Live Demo: Voice Engine Custom Voice Cloning
sections.summary: Huet records a few seconds of his voice and uses Voice Engine to generate a custom voice clone that narrates the Sora script in English, French, and Japanese, demonstrating multimodal chaining. Voice Engine is not broadly available due to safety considerations.

sections.title: Closing Remarks
sections.summary: Huet recaps the four focus areas and emphasizes OpenAI's goal is for developers to build more, not spend more. He frames this as the early innings of software 2.0 and encourages developers to bet on the future of AI.
